restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes: one root block, flags 11, block length 64, counter 0; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds.
2^96 groups of 2^32 messages; each group shares fresh uniform words m0..m14 and enumerates m15 = 0..2^32-1; N = 2^128 messages in one pass, no restart.
Each message is evaluated by a counted 247-operation word-RAM program that reuses group-invariant intermediate values; only the final verification invokes whole compressions (2 units).
Collision detection uses an uninitialised sparse-set table indexed by the top 140 digest bits; every operation is charged at 1/C with C = 430 (collision-frontier-v5).
Classical 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers and three-address operations; Section 9 of proof.md gives the bound if all group constants are reloaded per message (2^127.5419).
Score-critical heuristic H1 (grouped digests behave like independent uniform values for the collision events used); success 0.39 includes a 0.0033 allowance below the model value 0.3933.
Generic constant-factor improvement from amortisation, not a structural weakness of BLAKE3; the nominal reference identifier is metadata, not a claimed improvement over a qualified baseline.

heuristics.statement: For the N = 2^128 messages of the algorithm (2^96 groups, each with fresh uniform prefix words m0..m14 and m15 = 0..2^32-1), the probability that the 2-round BLAKE3 digests contain no equal pair, plus the probability of event F2 in proof.md Section 6 (a colliding pair whose first member was displaced by an earlier message with the same top 140 digest bits), exceeds the independent-uniform-model value 0.606654 by at most 0.0033.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the submitted grouped message family and sparse-set table: single 64-byte root blocks, uniform 480-bit group prefixes, consecutive m15 within a group, 256-bit digests, index width 140.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the scaled analogues (20-bit masked events with N_t = 2^10, organizer seeds; 32-bit events with N_t = 2^16, local seeds), in which N_t^2/2^w equals N^2/2^256 = 1, to the full 256-bit event with N = 2^128 and group size 2^32.
heuristics.limitations: Masked projections of the digest are tested, not the full 256-bit event. Organizer seeds are public, not a blinded holdout. Finite frequencies support but do not prove the population bound. Same-y cross-group pairs have a provable collision probability >= 2^-256; other pairs rely on H1.
